Description: Establish the platform security foundation for LexIA, including authentication, session management, numeric role enforcement, firm membership boundaries, password recovery, user administration, and auditable access-sharing behavior. This epic ensures that only authorized users can enter the system and only within the scope permitted by their role and firm context.
Acceptance Criteria: Successful login and protected access paths exist for each business role.
Definition of Done: Role model, auth flows, and authorization rules are implemented and testable.
Related Endpoints: POST /auth/register, POST /auth/login, POST /auth/refresh, POST /auth/password-recovery, POST /auth/password-reset, GET /users, POST /users, PATCH /users/{user_id}, DELETE /users/{user_id}, POST /cases/{id}/share, GET /cases/{id}/share

Description: Implement the core expediente domain, including case creation, ownership, lifecycle management, controlled visibility, and preserved operational history. This epic defines how legal matters are created, updated, transitioned, and later inspected without losing traceability.
Definition of Done: Users can create, view, update, close, archive, and inspect history for their cases.
Labels: Case CRUD and timeline behavior work end to end.

Description: Implement the document pipeline that receives case files, validates and stores them, preserves versions, runs OCR or extraction where needed, and transforms content into searchable case knowledge. This epic is responsible for converting uploaded evidence into a reliable retrieval layer while preserving strict case isolation.
Definition of Done: Supported documents become searchable case knowledge with visible processing states.
Labels: Upload to indexed knowledge flow works with auditability.

Description: Implement the retrieval-augmented generation capabilities for legal analysis and chat, with hard enforcement that every released answer is grounded in verifiable case and corpus citations. This epic covers retrieval, citation verification, generation control, persistence, and failure handling when evidence is insufficient or unverifiable.
Definition of Done: All AI outputs are grounded and blocked when citations are not verifiable.
Labels: Analysis and chat release only validated grounded responses.
column17: POST /cases/{id}/analyses, GET /cases/{id}/analyses/{analysis_id}, POST /chat/conversations, GET /chat/conversations/{id}, POST /chat/conversations/{id}/messages, PATCH /chat/conversations/{id}

Description: Implement the drafting and export layer that transforms verified legal context into editable documents such as tutela and derecho de peticion, and packages outputs into PDF or DOCX with the required metadata and disclaimers. This epic bridges AI-assisted generation with user-controlled editing and formal output delivery.
Definition of Done: Legal drafts are editable and exports include required metadata and disclaimer.
Labels: Draft generation and export work end to end.

Description: Implement the final hardening layer for the MVP, covering regression coverage, auditability validation, release criteria, and pilot readiness checks across all critical workflows. This epic ensures the product can be evaluated, tested, and released with confidence rather than only functionally demonstrated.
Definition of Done: Critical user flows, ACL checks, and release gates are validated before pilot launch.
Labels: Regression suite, test data, and release checklist are complete.
column17: Cross-cutting: auth, users, cases, documents, analyses, chat, drafts, export, history endpoints

Description: Implement the base authentication flow for platform users, including credential validation, session issuance, and tenant-safe authorization boundaries. This story covers register, login, refresh, status-based access checks, and the guarantee that users only see their own workspace or explicitly granted data.
Acceptance Criteria: Given valid credentials, when I log in, then I receive a valid session. Given invalid credentials, when I log in, then access is denied. Given status = false, when a user tries to log in, then access is denied. Given another user's case, when I try to access it without permission, then I receive 403.
Definition of Done: Auth endpoints, session management, status checks, and authorization tests are complete.

Description: Implement the authorization flow that lets a firm admin share a case with another permitted user while preserving auditability and firm boundaries. The story includes access-grant creation, permission-level storage, denial rules for unauthorized actors, and traceability of who granted access and when.
Definition of Done: Given a firm admin, when access is granted, then the grant is stored. Given a non-admin, when trying to share, then the request is denied. Given a grant, when access is used, then the event is auditable.
Labels: Sharing API, permission model, and audit entries are implemented.

Description: Implement a secure password recovery flow that allows users to regain access without exposing whether an email is registered. This story includes token generation, expiration rules, single-use enforcement, password reset validation, and a response model that avoids user enumeration.
Definition of Done: Given a registered email, when I request recovery, then the system responds without exposing whether the email exists. Given a valid recovery token, when I submit a new password, then the password is updated. Given an invalid or expired token, when I try to reset, then the request is rejected.
Labels: Password recovery and reset endpoints are implemented with token expiry, single use, and tests.

Description: Implement administrative user management for super admins and firm admins, covering user creation, listing, update, deactivation, and firm assignment. This story aligns the platform with the current contract where role_id is numeric from 1 to 3, status is boolean, password_hash is internal only, and visibility is restricted by tenant and firm scope.
Definition of Done: Given an authorized admin, when creating a user, then role_id accepts only values 1 to 3 and status is stored as boolean. Given a user list request, when filters are applied, then users are returned within the visible tenant or firm boundary. Given a deactivation request, when applied, then the user loses access without deleting audit history.
Labels: User CRUD endpoints, visibility rules, and deactivation flow are implemented and testable.

Description: Implement the initial case creation flow so lawyers can open a valid expediente with the required business fields, ownership context, and default lifecycle values. This story covers both API and UI validation for name, legal area, description, visibility, and the assignment of the case to the authenticated owner or firm context.
Definition of Done: Given name and legal area, when I create the case, then it is stored. Given missing required fields, when I create the case, then validation fails. Given a created case, then status is Pendiente de analisis.
Labels: Case creation UI and API validation are complete.

Description: Implement the controlled lifecycle of a case, including valid transitions, archival and closure behavior, updated timestamps, and preservation of historical visibility. This story ensures status changes are deliberate, rule-based, and do not compromise the integrity or traceability of the expediente.
Definition of Done: Given an allowed transition, when I update status, then it persists. Given a closed or archived case, then history remains accessible.
Labels: Lifecycle rules are implemented and tested.

Description: Implement the user-facing document intake flow for cases, allowing supported files to be uploaded, validated, stored, and tracked through visible processing states. This story covers the connection between upload actions and the backend processing pipeline so users understand what has been received and what is still being processed.
Definition of Done: Given unsupported formats or oversize files, upload is rejected. Given a valid file, then a document record and version are created. Given processing starts, then status updates are visible.
Labels: Upload flow, validation, and status updates work end to end.

Description: Implement OCR and extraction quality handling for scanned or image-based documents so uploaded evidence becomes analyzable when possible and is explicitly blocked when quality is too poor. This story covers asynchronous extraction, status changes, and the business rule that low-quality content cannot be used for analysis.
Definition of Done: Given a scanned PDF, when processing runs, then OCR is attempted. Given low-quality extraction, then status becomes Calidad insuficiente. Given insufficient quality, then analysis is blocked.
Labels: OCR pipeline and quality gate are implemented.

Description: Implement the legal analysis flow that produces structured outputs only when enough trustworthy case and corpus evidence exists. This story covers analysis requests, retrieval-backed generation, minimum citation requirements, required legal sections, and persistence of corpus version and disclaimer metadata.
Definition of Done: Given enough evidence, when analysis completes, then it includes all mandatory sections. Given completed analysis, then at least 3 norms and 2 rulings are cited. Given completed analysis, then corpus version and disclaimer are stored.
Labels: Analysis API, prompt flow, verifier, and persistence are complete.

Description: Implement the billing safeguard that refunds consumed credits when an analysis fails due to a technical platform error rather than a user or business-rule condition. This story ensures usage accounting remains fair, auditable, and reversible when the system itself cannot complete the requested operation.
Definition of Done: Given a technical failure, then analysis status records the failure. Given a consumed credit event, then a refund ledger entry is created.
Labels: Refund ledger behavior is implemented behind feature flag.

Description: Implement the legal chat flow so users can ask contextual questions and receive grounded answers only when citations are verifiable. This story includes question validation, retrieval, response generation, citation display, and suppression of answers that do not pass verification.
Definition of Done: Given a valid question length, when I ask, then the response includes citations. Given invalid length, then validation fails. Given unverifiable citations, then the response is withheld.
Labels: Chat flow returns verified cited responses only.

Description: Implement the ability to associate a conversation with a case while preserving strict separation between conversational activity and formal case state. This story ensures chat can be contextual to a matter without silently modifying case facts, ownership, or lifecycle fields.
Definition of Done: Given a linked conversation, then the link is stored. Given chat activity, then no automatic mutation of case data occurs.
Labels: Conversation linking and persistence are implemented.

Description: Implement the drafting flow for tutela documents so users can generate an initial version from case and analysis context and then refine it manually. This story combines structured generation with human editing rather than treating AI output as a final immutable result.
Definition of Done: Given prior analysis, when draft generation runs, then required sections are present. Given a generated draft, then I can edit it.
Labels: Tutela draft generation and editing are complete.

Description: Implement the drafting flow for derecho de peticion documents, including generation of required sections, applicable legal framing, and recipient-aware content that users can later edit before export or delivery.
Definition of Done: Given draft generation, then required sections are present. Given a recipient, then the applicable regime is identified.
Labels: Derecho de peticion draft generation is complete.

Summary: Analysis Export to PDF and DOCX
Description: Implement the export capability for completed analyses so users can produce formal deliverables in PDF or DOCX format with the required metadata, sources, and disclaimer language. This story turns structured results into shareable outputs without losing traceability.
Definition of Done: Given an analysis, when export completes, then the file includes case name, date, results, sources, and disclaimer.
Labels: Export generation and secured download work correctly.

Description: Implement the unified history timeline that lets users inspect the full sequence of relevant case activity, including uploads, analyses, chats, drafts, and sharing events. This story provides the traceability layer needed to understand how a matter evolved over time.
Definition of Done: Given a case, then analyses, chats, docs, generated docs, and share events appear chronologically.
Labels: History timeline is visible and consistent across event types.

Description: Build the core auth endpoints and services for register, login, and refresh, including password hashing, JWT creation and validation, role claims, and enforcement of the current user contract where role_id is limited to 1..3 and status is a boolean access flag.
Definition of Done: Endpoints, tests, and API docs are complete.

Summary: Build Flutter auth shell and route guards
Description: Build the frontend authentication shell, including sign-in screens, session persistence, route protection, token-aware startup flow, and redirects that prevent unauthenticated or unauthorized users from reaching protected sections of the application.
Definition of Done: Users can sign in and navigate only to authorized sections.

Summary: Model users firms and access policies
Description: Define the users and firms authorization model, including numeric role_id mapping, boolean user status handling, firm membership constraints, owner relationships, and middleware or service rules that block cross-tenant access by default.
Definition of Done: Role checks cover role_id values 1 to 3, boolean user status, and firm membership paths.
Related Endpoints: GET /users, POST /users, PATCH /users/{user_id}, DELETE /users/{user_id}, GET /cases, POST /cases, GET /cases/{id}, PATCH /cases/{id}, POST /cases/{id}/share, GET /cases/{id}/share

Summary: Implement case sharing API and audit logging
Description: Create the backend endpoints and persistence flow for granting, listing, and enforcing case access permissions. This task includes storing the granted user, permission level, granting actor, and audit events so every share action is traceable and reversible at the business level.
Definition of Done: Only firm admins can share and audit records are persisted.

Summary: Implement password recovery and reset endpoints
Description: Create the public auth endpoints for password recovery and password reset, including token issuance, expiration timestamps, single-use invalidation, minimum password validation, and a neutral recovery response that does not reveal whether an email exists.
Definition of Done: Recovery flow works end to end with validation and automated tests.

Summary: Align auth and user schemas with current contract
Description: Refactor request and response schemas, DTOs, and validation rules so auth and user payloads match the latest specification: role_id as integer 1 through 3, status as boolean, and no password_hash exposure in public responses.
Definition of Done: Schemas, validation rules, and examples match the API specification.
Related Endpoints: POST /auth/register, POST /auth/login, POST /auth/refresh, POST /auth/password-recovery, POST /auth/password-reset, GET /users, POST /users, PATCH /users/{user_id}, DELETE /users/{user_id}

Description: Create the administrative user management endpoints for listing, creating, updating, and deactivating users. The API must enforce admin-only access, tenant-safe filtering, firm-aware visibility rules, soft-delete behavior through status, and omission of password_hash from all public payloads.
Definition of Done: User management endpoints pass API tests and never expose password_hash.

Summary: Implement users and firms persistence model
Description: Create the persistence layer, migrations, or repository contracts for users and firms based on the agreed schema: unique email, indexed firm-role access, nullable firm_id, password_hash storage, boolean status, and ownership references needed for firm administration.
Definition of Done: Users and firms schema supports role_id, firm_id, boolean status, and documented indexes.

Description: Build the admin-facing user management interface with searchable user lists, create and edit forms, status toggles, role selectors, and deactivation actions. The UI should expose only allowed controls for authorized admins and mirror the API validation rules for role_id, firm membership, and status.
Definition of Done: Authorized admins can manage users from the UI with proper validation feedback.

Description: Create the backend endpoints for creating, listing, retrieving, and updating cases, including validation for required fields, ownership assignment, firm scoping, and default values such as initial status and visibility flags. The task also covers API tests and error handling for unauthorized access.
Definition of Done: Case CRUD passes API tests and enforces required fields.

Summary: Build case list detail and create screens
Description: Build the frontend flows for case creation and navigation, including the case list, case detail view, required-field forms, loading states, empty states, and validation feedback so users can create and review their matters end to end from the UI.
Definition of Done: Users can create and browse cases from the UI.

Description: Implement the business rules that govern case status changes, including allowed transitions, archive and close behavior, updated timestamps, and persistence rules that preserve history and prevent invalid mutations on inactive or completed matters.
Definition of Done: Lifecycle transitions enforce allowed states and preserve data.

Summary: Build case status controls in UI
Description: Add case lifecycle controls to the frontend detail view, including status change actions, confirmation prompts, disabled states for invalid transitions, and clear success or error feedback so users understand when and why a case can change state.
Definition of Done: Users can move cases through allowed statuses from the UI.

Summary: Implement document upload API and object storage integration
Description: Create the document intake API for multipart uploads, file-type and file-size validation, object storage writes, and metadata persistence tied to the owning case. The task includes rejecting unsupported or unsafe files and returning the initial processing state needed by downstream workers.
Definition of Done: Supported files upload successfully and invalid files are rejected.

Summary: Build document upload and status UI
Description: Build the frontend document intake experience with upload controls, file validation messaging, document listing, and visible processing states so users can submit files and monitor whether they are pending, processing, insufficient, or ready for analysis.
Definition of Done: Users can upload files and monitor status transitions.

Description: Implement the backend model and persistence rules for non-destructive document versioning, including current-version pointers, historical retention, and case-linked metadata so updates or replacements do not erase prior uploaded evidence.
Definition of Done: Document history preserves prior versions.

Description: Build the asynchronous OCR and text extraction worker for scanned PDFs and image-heavy documents, including job pickup, extraction execution, raw output persistence, and status updates that feed the document processing pipeline.
Definition of Done: Scanned documents are OCR-processed asynchronously.

Description: Create the quality evaluation stage for extracted document text, including heuristics or scoring rules that detect unreadable output, low-confidence extraction, or incomplete content and mark those documents as insufficient for analysis.
Definition of Done: Low-quality documents are blocked from analysis with clear status.

Summary: Implement chunking embeddings and pgvector indexing
Description: Build the document post-processing stage that splits extracted text into chunks, generates embeddings, attaches case metadata, and stores vectors in pgvector so retrieval remains searchable and isolated by case and source.
Definition of Done: Processed documents become searchable chunks isolated by case.

Summary: Ingest legal corpus metadata and chunks
Description: Load the legal reference corpus, including norms and jurisprudence, into the source registry and vector storage with version metadata, source identifiers, and searchable text so the analysis pipeline can retrieve authoritative legal context.
Definition of Done: Corpus entries are searchable and versioned.

Summary: Build retrieval orchestration and citation verifier
Description: Implement the orchestration layer that retrieves evidence from both case knowledge and the legal corpus, composes candidate context for generation, and verifies that returned citations are real, relevant, and attributable before any response is released.
Definition of Done: Only verified sources appear in analysis results.

Description: Create the backend API and execution flow for requesting legal analyses, dispatching asynchronous processing, polling status, and persisting structured output sections, citations, corpus version, disclaimers, and failure reasons when generation cannot be completed.
Definition of Done: Analysis results persist required sections, citations, corpus version, and disclaimer.

Description: Build the frontend experience for requesting, monitoring, and reading legal analyses, including action triggers, loading and failure states, status polling, and structured rendering of sections, warnings, citations, and disclaimers.
Definition of Done: Users can request and review legal analysis from the UI.

Summary: Implement credit ledger and refund workflow
Description: Implement the internal credit accounting flow for analysis execution, including debit events, failure classification, and automatic refund behavior for technical failures behind a feature flag so billing logic remains auditable and reversible.
Definition of Done: Refund events are created only on technical failures.

Description: Create the backend conversation and message APIs with persistence for messages, participants, timestamps, and optional case links so legal chat can be resumed, audited, and connected to a matter without mutating case data automatically.
Definition of Done: Chat messages persist with linkage to conversations and optional case IDs.

Summary: Implement chat generation with verified citations
Description: Implement the AI chat execution flow that performs retrieval, grounded response generation, citation validation, and persistence of the final answer and supporting sources, blocking delivery whenever the citation verifier cannot confirm the result.
Definition of Done: Chat responses are blocked unless citations are verified.

Description: Build the frontend legal chat interface with conversation list, message composer, streaming or pending states if applicable, citation display, and error handling so users can ask questions and review grounded answers in a usable conversation flow.
Definition of Done: Users can send legal questions and inspect cited answers.

Description: Implement the backend rules and persistence for optionally linking a conversation to a case while explicitly preventing chat activity from silently updating case facts, status, ownership, or other case metadata.
Definition of Done: Conversations can be linked to cases without changing case facts or status.

Description: Implement the generation workflow for tutela drafts, using case context, verified analysis output, and relevant jurisprudence to produce editable structured content that includes the mandatory legal sections required by the business domain.
Definition of Done: Tutela drafts include required sections and remain editable.

Description: Build the frontend draft editing workspace with editable content areas, save interactions, draft retrieval, and export entry points so users can review and modify generated legal drafts before finalizing them.
Definition of Done: Users can edit generated drafts before export.

Summary: Implement derecho de peticion generation flow
Description: Implement the generation workflow for derecho de peticion documents, including recipient-aware content, legal basis assembly, and applicable regime identification so the draft output follows the required structure and can later be edited or exported.
Definition of Done: Derecho de peticion drafts include required content and regime selection.

Description: Implement the backend export flow that renders analysis or drafting outputs into PDF and DOCX, injects disclaimer and source metadata, stores generated files securely, and returns controlled download references suitable for authenticated access.
Definition of Done: Exports render correctly and are stored securely.

Description: Create the backend aggregation API that collects case-related events from documents, analyses, chats, drafts, and sharing activity into a single chronological feed with actor metadata, event typing, and stable ordering for frontend consumption.
Definition of Done: History API returns complete ordered case activity.

Description: Build the frontend timeline view that renders the aggregated case history feed with event grouping, timestamps, actor information, and event-specific presentation so users can inspect how a case evolved over time.
Definition of Done: Users can review full case evolution from the UI.

Summary: Create end-to-end regression suite and release checklist
Description: Create the QA regression suite and release-readiness checklist covering authentication, sharing, document intake, OCR, analysis, chat, drafting, export, and history so the team can validate critical pilot flows consistently before each release.
Definition of Done: Critical paths have repeatable test coverage and release checklist sign-off.
Related Endpoints: Cross-cutting: auth, users, cases, documents, analyses, chat, drafts, export, history endpoints
